I checked each claim in the draft against the policy.

- "Good tea, no fuss." This is plain and warm, and it isn't a superlative. "Good" is a mild descriptor, not a "best" or "finest" claim. Fine.
- "Certified organic by the Soil Association" matches the allowlist wording exactly. Certificate renewed 2026, so it's current.
- "packed by hand in Bristol" is a slight shortening of "Every tin is packed by hand in Bristol". It says the same thing and doesn't overstate it. Fine.
- "free UK delivery on orders over £25" matches the allowlist wording exactly.
- Voice: UK spelling, no banned words, no urgency, no health or environmental claims, no invented numbers.
- Disclosure: this is our own landing page, so no label is needed.

Nothing needs changing. Approval: Sam (marketing lead) signs off on all public content, so it should go to Sam before it is published.
